body:
### Problem

`vim.pack.add()` activates plugins through `:packadd`, which repeats package discovery across `'packpath'` for each plugin. This adds measurable startup overhead even for empty packages, before any plugin code is executed.

In `src/nvim/runtime.c`, `ex_packadd()` performs:

- A `pack/*/start/{name}` search if start packages have not yet been sourced.
- A `pack/*/opt/{name}` search.

Both searches use `do_in_path()` with `DIP_ALL`, so they visit every entry in `'packpath'`. Wildcard expansion scans the existing `pack/` directories again for each package. The start search commonly happens during `init.lua`, but is skipped if packages have already been sourced, for example by an earlier `:packloadall`.

`vim.pack` already knows each managed plugin's directory and only manages optional packages. The existing incremental runtime-search-cache update is present in the tested revision; these repeated discovery scans still occur.

### Steps to reproduce

Save this as `packadd-repro.lua`:

```lua
local root, n = vim.fn.tempname(), 20
for i = 1, n do
  vim.fn.mkdir(root .. '/pack/core/opt/startup_bench_' .. i .. '/plugin', 'p')
end
vim.opt.packpath:prepend(root)
vim.api.nvim_get_runtime_file('lua/nonexistent_startup_benchmark.lua', false)

local start = vim.uv.hrtime()
for i = 1, n do
  vim.cmd.packadd({ 'startup_bench_' .. i, bang = true })
end
local elapsed = (vim.uv.hrtime() - start) / 1e6
print(('packadd!: %.3f ms/package (%d packages, %d packpath entries)'):format(
  elapsed / n, n, #vim.opt.packpath:get()
))
vim.fn.delete(root, 'rf')
```

Run before normal startup package loading:

```sh
nvim --clean --headless --cmd 'luafile packadd-repro.lua' +qa
```

The fixture creates empty optional packages and warms the runtime search cache before measuring `:packadd!`. Package creation and cleanup are outside the timed section. Repeat in fresh processes to compare startup behavior.

### Expected behavior

Activating managed optional packages should avoid unnecessary repeated discovery work while preserving runtime-path ordering and package-loading behavior.

### Nvim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-521eddec7c

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

N/A

### Operating system/version

macOS 27.0

### Terminal name/version

Ghostty 1.3.1

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-ghostty

### Installation

build from repo

comment_data.body:
I have two alternative implementations for discussion, both based on 521eddec7c243a8166609bf1734cb940e9510fc5. They are independent, not intended to be stacked. Both leave generic `:packadd` behavior unchanged.

**1. Load managed packages by their known directory**

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/42107

`vim.pack` passes the directory it already knows to a private package-loading entry point. This skips both discovery globs and reuses the existing runtime path insertion, cache update, and plugin/ftdetect loading code. Manifest scripts use the same path; existing `after/plugin` handling is retained.

The behavior change is deliberate: `vim.pack` activates only its managed directory, rather than also activating other packages with the same name. It also works when the managed data site is absent from `'packpath'`.

**2. Restrict discovery to optional packages**

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/42108

`vim.pack` uses a private opt-only entry point into the shared package-loading code. It skips the start-package search but still searches all of `'packpath'` for matching optional packages, retaining all matches and their ordering.

This preserves more of the existing discovery behavior, including the `'packpath'` requirement and loading multiple same-named opt packages. A same-named start package is left to normal startup loading instead of being activated by `vim.pack`.

**Comparison**

Using binaries built from the same base with identical build settings, the 20-package benchmark gave these medians across 12 fresh processes per variant, after warmup and with execution order rotated:

| Activation method | Time per package | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline `:packadd!` | 0.518 ms | — |
| Exact-path loading | 0.134 ms | 74% |
| Opt-only discovery | 0.314 ms | 39% |

**3. Cache package-directory listings — not implemented**

A third option is to cache the `pack/*` listings for each `'packpath'` entry and reuse them across package lookups. This could also benefit ordinary `:packadd`, beyond `vim.pack`.

I have not implemented or benchmarked this option because it first needs a reliable invalidation strategy. Directories can be created, removed, or replaced without changing `'packpath'`, running `:packloadall`, or going through `vim.pack`. In particular, a new same-named package can appear after a successful lookup, so refreshing only on cache misses would still change the current all-matches behavior.

Caching remains an option, but preserving that behavior requires more filesystem freshness handling than either of the two alternatives above. I started with those to provide measurable improvements without introducing a persistent discovery cache.

Which direction would be preferable?

To me both #42107 and #42108 look like adding too much for a small gain. The intent behind using plain `:packadd` is that it uses tried and tested approach to loading plugins. I'd be hesitant about adding custom private loading functions that will be used in `vim.pack` only. *Maybe* it might be worth it if 74% gain is confirmed (which I personally doubht), but that requires careful (manual, not LLM assisted) performance benchmarks.

If I had to choose, loading by known path is faster with roughly the same complexity, so that looks better. But in any way, I'd rather wait for this to be merged *after* 0.13 release and *only* after a more careful review from someone more knowledgeable about C and `:packadd` code (like @bfredl).

milestone.description: We don't plan to work on this, but will accept high quality contributions from someone who will own the feature and follow up on bug reports.
